paper_metadata.title: A performance characterization of quantum generative models

summary: The paper benchmarks quantum generative models (QCBM and QGAN) on 2D and 3D datasets using up to 12 qubits and circuits with up to ~174 gates on statevector simulators. Across >1200 experiments, discrete copula architectures with PIT preprocessing achieved the best performance, e.g., KL ≈ 0.029 for a 3D X dataset with 54 parameters, compared with a classical GAN achieving KL ≈ 0.089 with 9475 parameters. The work shows parameter-efficiency advantages for some datasets but no demonstrated computational quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Benchmark of quantum circuit Born machines (QCBM) for generative modeling on low-dimensional synthetic and real financial datasets using continuous, discrete standard, and discrete copula circuit architectures.

algorithm.variant: QCBM generative modeling with continuous, discrete standard, and discrete copula ansatzes
algorithm.ansatz: continuous data-reuploading circuit; discrete standard circuit; discrete copula circuit
algorithm.convergence_criteria: maximum number of epochs/iterations reached or KL divergence change below threshold (threshold not specified)
algorithm.parameter_initialization: subsequent circuit blocks initialized from previously fitted blocks; new block parameters initialized to zero / identity
algorithm.hyperparameters.qubits_for_continuous: 1 qubit per data dimension (2 qubits for 2D datasets, 3 qubits for 3D datasets)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: discrete architectures discretize each data dimension with 4 qubits (16 grid points per dimension); continuous architecture uses one qubit per data dimension and outputs expectation values of Pauli-Z
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize KL divergence between training-data histogram Q and model distribution P(θ)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: copula architecture enforced via initial maximally entangled state and no inter-register entangling gates after initialization; PIT preprocessing used for copula learning

problem_instance.description: Generative modeling of synthetic and real low-dimensional distributions
problem_instance.dataset_name: Mixture of Gaussian distributions, X-shaped distribution, O-shaped distribution, Stocks

ticker_symbols: Yahoo Finance stock pricing data (tickers not specified)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: For each dataset, data were transformed using either min-max normalization to [0,1] or PIT to learn the copula; stocks used daily returns from Yahoo Finance close prices
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each experiment repeated 5 times; performance reported as KL divergence and minimum KL over runs

implementation_details.code_url: open-sourced simulation library qugen (URL not provided)
implementation_details.classical_solver: CMA-ES for QCBM optimization; classical neural network baseline also used
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: min-max normalization or PIT; histogramming of data distributions
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: KL divergence evaluation; synthetic sample generation from trained model

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: KL generally decreases with more parameters and training epochs; discrete copula/PIT often most stable

speedup_claims.factor: up to two orders of magnitude fewer parameters
speedup_claims.conditions: for some datasets, especially O and X in 2D/3D; based on parameter count rather than runtime
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a parameter-efficiency claim, not a proven runtime or asymptotic speedup. The paper explicitly states no quantum advantage is demonstrated.

speedup_claims.factor: similar or fewer parameters than classical counterparts
speedup_claims.conditions: across all datasets; best case reported for 3D X where QGAN with 54 parameters achieved KL 0.029 vs classical GAN with 9475 parameters and KL 0.089
speedup_claims.caveats: Comparison is on simulator and uses KL divergence; not a hardware speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: paper states experiments do not demonstrate that simulated quantum circuits go beyond current classical GAN capabilities

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Runtime/sample scales linearly with data dimension d; continuous: O(Ns·Nb·(d+4)); discrete standard: O(Nb·(rd+2)); discrete copula: O(r(d−1)+1 + Nb(r(r−1)/2 + 3))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly characterized asymptotically; classical GAN baseline scales with hidden-layer size and depth

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; experiments limited to 2D–3D datasets with ≤12 qubits
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Authors estimate real applications with ~100‑dimensional data would require ~100 qubits for continuous circuits or ~1600 qubits for discrete copula architectures (r=16 discretization)
limiting_factors: Experiments performed only on noiseless statevector simulators
Problem sizes extremely small (2–3 dimensional distributions)
No asymptotic quantum speedup claimed or demonstrated
Sampling overhead for continuous architecture due to shot requirements

notes: Hardware is a state-vector simulator because the paper explicitly states all experiments were run on Qiskit and PennyLane state-vector simulators.
Exact total gate counts are only partially reported; appendix provides per-block formulas and discussion mentions up to 174 gates overall.
Authors explicitly state current quantum devices do not surpass classical counterparts.
Quantum models sometimes require fewer parameters than classical GANs but do not demonstrate computational advantage.

experiments.description: Benchmark of quantum generative adversarial networks (QGAN) with a quantum generator and classical discriminator on the same datasets, comparing continuous, discrete standard, and discrete copula architectures.

algorithm.variant: QGAN with quantum generator and classical discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: continuous data-reuploading circuit; discrete standard circuit; discrete copula circuit
algorithm.optimizer: gradient descent; Optax/JAX for continuous, parameter-shift-based gradient descent for discrete
algorithm.convergence_criteria: training for a fixed number of epochs; convergence judged by KL divergence and training stability
algorithm.parameter_initialization: QGANs were cold-started; no lower-depth initialization used
algorithm.hyperparameters.qubits_for_continuous: 1 qubit per data dimension (2 qubits for 2D datasets, 3 qubits for 3D datasets)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: discrete architectures use 4 qubits per dimension; continuous architecture uses one qubit per dimension and outputs expectation values; generator samples are fed to a classical discriminator
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize GAN cross-entropy losses for generator and discriminator; performance evaluated by KL divergence to training distribution
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: copula architecture via entangled initialization and no inter-register entangling gates after initialization; PIT preprocessing for copula learning
